subject: Releasing parameter constraints in MGCFA with three groups

messages.author: 5c527df876dd0445
messages.subject: Releasing parameter constraints in MGCFA with three groups
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to run a multigroup model to test measurement invariance. There are three groups (lets call them groups A, B, and C) in my data set and I am facing two issues. I believe they are easy to address but they are new to me and I am unsure of how should I set the model arguments:

----
First issue:

I have a model like

'f =~ V1 + V2 + V3'

and I want to constraint loadings to equality across groups A, B, and C. After inspecting model fit and MI indices, I need to free the loading of V3 in group C only in order to improve model fit (and achieve partial measurement invariance). If I simply include

group.equal = c("loadings"),
group.partial = c("f=~V3")

the loading for V3 in group B is also freed. I think I can go around this setting the model like

'f =~ V1 + V2 + c(lo1,lo1,NA)*V3'

but I wonder if there is any to do it using 'group.partial'?


----
Second issue:

Assume I have the same model and groups as above but now V1, V2, and V3 are categorical (four-point likert scales, with three thresholds each) and I run a model using WLSMV estimator.

I am testing invariance of thresholds and found that, in order to achieve an acceptable model fit, I need to free the following parameters:
- threshold2 in variable V3 in group B; and
- threshold3 in variable V3 in group C.

If I add the arguments:

group.equal = c("loadings", "thresholds"),
group.partial = c("V3|t2", "V3|t3")

I will be setting V3|t2 as a free parameter for both groups B and C at the same time, being the same true for V3|t3 -- and this is *not* what I intend to do.


How do I allow a threshold to be freely estimated for a specific group, either using 'group.partial' or via model syntax?



Thank you a lot!

Fabricio

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Releasing parameter constraints in MGCFA with three groups
parts:
I think I can go around this setting the model like
'f =~ V1 + V2 + c(lo1,lo1,NA)*V3'
Yes, that is the way to do it.
but I wonder if there is any to do it using 'group.partial'?
No, not that I am aware of.  The group.equal and group.partial arguments are for convenience in simple situations, but using model syntax is more reliable in more nuanced situations.
How do I allow a threshold to be freely estimated for a specific group, either using 'group.partial' or via model syntax?

Here is what the syntax would look like:

V3 | c(arbitraryLabel1, NA, arbitraryLabel1)*t2
V3 | c(arbitraryLabel2, arbitraryLabel2, NA)*t3
